Marathon Petroleum stock: DBS Bank cuts rating to Hold
sum: DBS Bank downgraded Marathon Petroleum from Moderate Buy to Hold, according to a MarketBeat report published Thursday, November 26, 2026. The change introduces a more cautious analyst stance toward the refiner even as the wider analyst view remains positive.

MarketBeat said the bank moved its rating from Moderate Buy to Hold in a research note issued to investors. The report did not identify a new price target from DBS Bank, while the broader analyst consensus remained Moderate Buy.

MarketBeat cited a consensus price target of USD 417.62 based on 18 ratings, including 11 Buy ratings and seven Hold ratings. The mix suggests that the downgrade changes the tone for Marathon Petroleum without overturning the prevailing positive view among covered analysts.

The rating change follows Marathon Petroleum's strong third-quarter performance. MarketBeat reported adjusted earnings per share of USD 26.93, above the USD 25.37 analyst estimate, while revenue reached USD 56.03 billion and increased 57.6 percent from the prior-year quarter.

For investors, the downgrade puts greater emphasis on whether the company's unusually strong refining performance can persist. The contrast between the Hold call from DBS Bank and the Moderate Buy consensus leaves future margin trends, operating execution and estimate revisions as important factors for the shares.
Investors can follow broader market developments in the current market reports.

sum: Trade rules are tightening, yet global commerce still moves trillions across borders, and that mix of friction and flow can reshape which trade finance stocks thrive or struggle. Investors watching record-high restrictions and fresh support measures may see both risk and missed potential. This article explains those dynamics and profiles 3 trade-focused stocks exposed to these global shifts, helping you decide which may deserve a closer look now.

The three stocks below are just a starting sample of trade-finance and trade-credit insurance providers. The full screen surfaced 69 more companies with equally compelling narratives that are not covered here. To go straight to the wider opportunity set, use the Global Trade-Finance and Trade-Credit Insurance Providers screener to identify, filter and analyze the trade-focused ideas that best fit your own thesis.
Absa Group is a pan African banking and insurance group that fits this trade finance theme through its corporate, investment banking and trade focused services across cross border corridors.

Absa Group runs a broad banking, insurance and wealth platform, linking retail clients and corporates into African and global trade flows. Revenue is mainly sourced from South Africa at ZAR82.4b and Africa Regions at ZAR35.6b, with a market value of roughly ZAR169.8b.

The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St frames Absa Group as a trade connected lender that is trying to shift more of its earnings towards pan African fee and client activity income, rather than relying mainly on domestic interest sensitive revenue.

Accelerated expansion and integration of Absa Group's pan African operations is still expected to diversify earnings beyond South Africa, with Africa Regions contributing 31% of group earnings in 2025 and management continuing to position these markets as a larger share of group revenue and earnings over time.

DBS upbeat despite earnings miss, global uncertainty
sum: SINGAPORE: Singapore’s DBS Group warned yesterday of heightened uncertainty due to geopolitical risks, high energy costs and borrowing rates, but remained upbeat about its outlook despite a plunge in trading income that dragged down earnings. DBS, Southeast Asia’s biggest lender by assets, said July-September net profit fell 5% to S$2.81 billion (RM8.9 billion) from ​a year earlier. The result undershot the mean estimate of S$2.9 billion from four analysts, according to LSEG data, even though its wealth management division ‌posted a strong performance. The group’s markets trading income sank 65% year-on-year to S$152 million, which DBS ​attributed to “unfavourable equity market conditions”. That contrasted with Wall Street and European peers, whose equity desks benefited from a surge in market activity, while fixed-income trading lagged. “The US peers did very well because they had large prime brokerage and prime businesses. We don’t have that at the moment, but we’ll see,“ DBS CEO Tan Su Shan said on an earnings call. She added that ​the lender was building up its financial institutions and institutional investors coverage. Tan said trading income also fell due to weaker Asian asset performance, a surge in global bond yields and a ‌drop in trading volume. The decline ​underscores how surging global bond yields, a rout in high-flying technology stocks and the ongoing Middle East ​conflict are beginning to bite into Singapore lenders’ earnings after wealth management momentum cushioned their bottom lines in the first half. Shares of DBS ​fell more than 2% early yesterday following the results, though later pared losses to trade 0.3% lower. The bank’s net interest margin (NIM), a key profitability gauge, fell 9 basis points year-on-year to 1.87%. The results from DBS came a day after its smaller peer UOB posted a fall in its trading and investment income and flagged further margin pressures ahead. DBS, however, struck a more upbeat tone, expecting its September exit NIM of 1.9% to be largely sustained in the fourth quarter. Tan said the bank was ‌also expecting a “healthy loan pipeline” in 2027 and total income to rise in the mid-single-digit range.

items.t: Review: DBS Vantage Card
sum: DBS was a relatively late entrant to the S$120K segment, only launching the DBS Vantage Card in June 2022. With rivals having many more years to build up a customer base, it was always going to be playing catch-up.

Therefore, it needed to start strong, and that’s exactly what it did, with a generous 80,000 miles sign-up offer, a limited-time 4 mpd on dining and petrol, a complimentary Accor Plus membership and 10 lounge visits.

Fast forward to today, and things are less rosy. There hasn’t been a welcome offer in more than a year, the option to waive the annual fee with S$60,000 in annual spend has been removed, and the local earn rate — once the best in the S$120K segment — was recently cut to 1.4 mpd.
But it’s a very different story for DBS Treasures customers, who now receive four airport limo rides, and even an annual fee waiver, if they have Accredited Investor (AI) status.
So is there still a case for “normies” getting a DBS Vantage Card then?
Let’s start this review by looking at the key features of the DBS Vantage Card.
The DBS Vantage Card comes in metal cardstock, and weighs 10g. That makes it one of the lighter metal cards on the market, if that sort of thing is important to you.

DBS Group stock: JPMorgan upgrades rating, raises target to SGD 82
sum: JPMorgan upgraded DBS Group Holdings from Neutral to Overweight on Thursday, November 19, and raised its price target from SGD 76 to SGD 82, according to Investing.com. The move followed a 15% retreat from the bank's October 2026 peak, which JPMorgan viewed as improving the valuation case.

The bank highlighted DBS's technology infrastructure, limited exposure to general commercial real estate, wealth-management operations, high payout ratio and hedging of US dollar interest-rate risk. JPMorgan expects DBS to trade above three times forward price-to-book by 2028 and projects an 18.1% return on equity for that year.

JPMorgan also pointed to a 0.9% non-performing-loan ratio, 124% coverage and a 14% common-equity-tier-one ratio. The figures support the view that balance-sheet quality and capital strength remain central to the investment case.
DBS Group Holdings stock traded at 46.45 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 15:12 CET on Friday, November 20. The quote is in euros and reflects the Lang & Schwarz market.

The rating change gives investors a fresh view on valuation after the October pullback. The main points to watch are whether DBS can convert its wealth-management and technology investments into recurring earnings while preserving asset quality and capital returns.

items.t: DBS Group stock: Circle partnership expands USDC access in Asia
sum: DBS Group and Circle announced on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, that they are expanding institutional access to USDC in Asia through a new partnership, according to the Circle press release. Eligible institutional clients will be able to mint and redeem the stablecoin directly through DBS rather than relying solely on secondary-market liquidity.
DBS Group stock traded at 47.30 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 09:32 CET on Wednesday, November 18, 2026.

The arrangement is designed to support treasury management, settlement and liquidity operations. It also enables 24/7 settlement between US dollars and USDC when clients mint or redeem through DBS, allowing institutions to move between fiat and digital-asset infrastructure outside traditional banking hours.

USDC is issued through Circle's regulated entities, while DBS contributes its institutional banking, liquidity and digital-asset capabilities in Asia. The structure gives corporate and financial clients a bank-based channel for stablecoin access and broadens the range of tokenized-money instruments available through the Singapore lender.

Circle's release cited a DBS report saying that 88% of large corporations were already deploying or piloting tokenized-money use cases, while more than three in five were adopting or planning to adopt stablecoins. The figures point to a growing institutional market for payment, treasury and settlement applications built on blockchain infrastructure.

Evy Theunis, DBS's head of digital assets for institutional banking, said the partnership combines Circle's regulated stablecoin infrastructure with DBS's banking, liquidity and digital-asset capabilities. Kash Razzaghi, Circle's chief commercial officer, described the cooperation as a step toward wider institutional access to USDC across Asia.

The partnership also builds on DBS and Circle's participation in Project BLOOM 2, an initiative led by the Monetary Authority of Singapore that focuses on interoperability between forms of tokenized money and financial networks. For DBS investors, the agreement reinforces the bank's digital-assets strategy and its role in institutional financial infrastructure, while the commercial importance will depend on client adoption and transaction activity.

DBS, JPMorgan’s Kinexys launch 24/7 transfers of tokenized deposits
sum: DBS and JPMorgan launched a service on Monday that lets clients transfer tokenized US dollar deposits between the two banks around the clock.

Tokenized deposits are bank deposits represented on the blockchain. The service connects DBS Token Services with JPMorgan’s Kinexys platform for transfers between Singapore and the US, according to a press release.
Ant International became the first client to use service to manage its cash across markets.

The launch supports the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s Project BLOOM, which aims to make it easier to use tokenized deposits and regulated stablecoins for payments in Singapore and across borders. The central bank launched the project in October 2025.

DBS and JPMorgan co-lead Project BLOOM’s working group on transfers between blockchain platforms. The two banks first revealed plans to develop a blockchain-based tokenization framework for onchain transfers in November 2025.
More than half of the 422 business leaders DBS surveyed across 11 markets said their companies used tokenized deposits or planned to do so, according to the bank’s Oct. 28 report.

Jensen Huang considering comeback as Nvidia CEO: FT, Money News
sum: Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia's chief executive, and has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning, the Financial Times reported on Sunday (Nov 15), citing people familiar with the matter.
One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia chief's return and would try to garner support from the White House.
"Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen," the person said, adding that the efforts had Huang's support.
The report comes days after the FT reported that Nvidia's board had approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside regular business hours.

Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy that raised questions over exports of the company's advanced AI chips to China. The scandal has plunged the chipmaker into crisis and sent shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll.

items.t: Primed for the next leap: The growing promise of Singapore’s fintechs
sum: The question is which of these firms will make it onto the local bourse, and how long they will take
[SINGAPORE] When iFast listed on the Singapore Exchange (SGX) mainboard in December 2014, few people would have called it a fintech.
It was an online fund platform with about S$5.6 billion in assets under administration (AUA) a year later, at a time when “fintech” was still a word heard mostly at conferences.

Today, its AUA stands at S$36.76 billion, up 20 per cent from a year ago, and the company runs a licensed bank in Britain. Since Oct 22, it also issues its own exchange-traded funds on the same bourse where its shares trade.
That makes iFast something of a veteran in a crowd of newcomers.

Singapore now has five digital banks, a pack of robo-advisers, lenders and payments firms that have spent years raising private money, and a government that has put money and rule changes behind getting growth companies to list at home.
The question for investors is which of these firms will make it onto the local bourse, and how long they will take.

items.t: New World Development Launches Massive "1-for-11" Rights Issue, Raising HK$24.9 Billion at Over 80% Discount
sum: New World Development (0017.HK) announced on Sunday evening (the 15th) that it proposes a fully underwritten rights issue on a "1-for-11" basis at HK$0.9 per rights share, aiming to raise gross proceeds of approximately HK$24.9 billion (approximately $3.2 billion). This is the core component of the group's comprehensive capital restructuring plan, combining the rights issue with a bank loan arrangement while simultaneously pursuing debt extension and deleveraging targets.

New World Development briefly suspended trading last Friday (the 13th) pending the release of inside information, after market speculation had already emerged that the group was preparing a rights issue. According to sources, the group's total debt stood at HK$143.3 billion (approximately $18.3 billion) as of the end of June this year, and the market has been closely watching its deleveraging and capital restructuring progress.
Rights Issue Must Clear Three Hurdles, Whitewash Waiver Is Key

The rights issue is conditional on the satisfaction of several conditions, including obtaining independent shareholder approval, being granted a whitewash waiver, and signing binding maturity extension agreements with all lenders under the target bank loans. Chow Tai Fook Enterprises has committed to subscribing in full for its rights entitlement and to providing further underwriting support.

New World Development Chairman and Executive Director Cheng Kar-shun said that by combining equity fundraising with debt maturity extension, the aim is to address short-term funding needs while giving the business greater flexibility to realize asset value in an orderly manner. He also noted that Chow Tai Fook Enterprises' commitment demonstrates its confidence in the group's long-term prospects.

A spokesperson for Chow Tai Fook Enterprises said the company is very confident in New World Development's prospects and fully supports its capital restructuring plan. The timing of this rights issue is ripe, and it also allows qualifying shareholders to participate equally in recovery and growth opportunities, and supports the group in resuming dividend payments in the future when financial performance and liquidity conditions are appropriate.

Colette Kress, the CFO who challenged Huang's bets, is Nvidia's interim CEO, Money News
sum: ВАШИНГТОН/САН-ФРАНЦИСКО – Колетт Кресс в течение многих лет была единственным руководителем Nvidia, желающим сдержать огромные, зачастую рискованные амбиции генерального директора Дженсена Хуанга. По словам двух человек, знакомых с этим вопросом, в четверг (12 ноября) он побудил производителя чипов глубже вложить многомиллиардные инвестиции в искусственный интеллект.

Теперь 59-летний финансовый директор временно получил высший пост, в то время как Nvidia ищет постоянного преемника. В четверг Хуанг ушел из компании, которую он соучредил и которой руководил в течение трех десятилетий в гуще скандала, оставив Nvidia осуществлять свою первую смену руководства без архитектора ее подъема.

По словам двух источников, в своих конфликтах Кресс служил важным противовесом Хуану, чей успех предоставил ему большую свободу в принятии ключевых решений. За несколько месяцев до новостей о том, что у Хуана были отношения с женщиной, подозреваемой в том, что она является китайской шпионкой, некоторые на Уолл-стрит задавались вопросом, разумен ли его аппетит к риску и способствуют ли сделки, которые он заключал, развитию все более замкнутой экономики искусственного интеллекта.

Кресс и ее сотрудники столкнулись с Хуанг и отделом продаж компании из-за масштабных и рискованных финансовых сделок, которые способствовали созданию того, что некоторые критики с Уолл-стрит считали циркулярной экономикой искусственного интеллекта, включая инвестиции в OpenAI и компании, занимающиеся инфраструктурой искусственного интеллекта, такие как Lambda, по словам одного из людей, знакомых с этим вопросом.

Предлагаемый план на сумму 250 миллиардов долларов США (322 миллиарда сингапурских долларов) для поддержки проекта центра обработки данных OpenAI в Огайо в конечном итоге был сокращен до 120 миллиардов долларов США.

«Я думаю, маловероятно, что кто-то, кроме Дженсена, будет так агрессивно инвестировать в своих клиентов», — сказал третий источник, венчурный инвестор. По словам этого человека, Хуанг подтолкнул Nvidia к предоставлению финансирования стартапам.

Люди, которые ее знают, описывают Кресс как успокаивающий контраст с часто конфронтационным стилем Хуана. Кресс присоединился к Nvidia в 2013 году после долгой карьеры в других гигантах технологической отрасли, включая Microsoft, Cisco и Texas Instruments.

sum: Shares in Singapore Telecommunications (Singtel) gained the most in three months after posting a 10 per cent rise in first-half underlying net profit on Friday, and raising its forecast for annual operating earnings from its core units.
Shares rose as much as three per cent in early trade, marking their biggest intraday gain since mid-August and outperforming the broader benchmark, which was down 0.4 per cent.
Southeast Asia's largest telecom operator said underlying net profit for the six months ended Sept 30 was $1.49 billion, up from $1.35 billion a year earlier.

Bolstered by the stellar first-half showing, Singtel now expects fiscal 2027 earnings before interest and tax for the operating company, excluding contributions from regional associates, to grow in the mid- to high-single digits, up from the previously forecast low- to mid-single-digit growth.

Operating revenue from Optus, Australia's second-largest telecommunications provider, which Singtel has owned since 2001, fell two per cent during the half-year, but stronger mobile performance and cost management translated into improved profitability.

Long a key earnings contributor for Singtel, Optus has faced a series of operational and reputational challenges in recent years, including cyber and network outages that sparked political and regulatory backlash.
Post-tax contributions from regional associates including India's Bharti Airtel, Thailand's Advanced Info Service (AIS) and Indonesia's Telkomsel rose nine per cent to $993 million.

sum: Singapore's largest bank, DBS Group, warned on Thursday of growing global uncertainty due to elevated energy prices, higher interest rates and geopolitical risks as market volatility pushed its earnings lower.

DBS, which is also Southeast Asia's biggest lender by assets, said July–September net profit fell 5 percent to S$2.81 billion (HK$17.26 billion) from a year earlier, mainly on a decline in markets trading income.
The result undershot the mean estimate of S$2.90 billion from four analysts, according to LSEG data, even though its wealth management division posted a strong performance.
The group's markets trading income sank 65 percent year-on-year to S$152 million for the quarter, which DBS attributed to "unfavourable equity market conditions".
The bank's net interest margin, a key profitability gauge, fell 9 basis points year-on-year to 1.87 percent.

The decline underscores how surging global bond yields, a rout in high-flying technology stocks last quarter and the ongoing Middle East conflict are beginning to bite into Singapore lenders' earnings after strong wealth management momentum cushioned their bottom lines in the first half.
Shares of DBS, which have risen 24 percent so far this year, fell more than 2 percent to S$69.27 in early trading.

sum: DBS Group reported lower third-quarter profit after a sharp decline in markets trading income outweighed growth in lending, wealth management and customer fees. In its third-quarter trading update dated November 5, DBS said net profit for the three months ended September 30 fell 5 percent year on year to SGD 2.813 billion. Profit was also 9 percent below the second quarter.

Total income declined 1 percent from a year earlier to SGD 5.845 billion and fell 4 percent sequentially. The main drag was markets trading income, which dropped 65 percent year on year to SGD 152 million amid unfavourable market conditions. Compared with the second quarter, the decline was 68 percent.

DBS said net interest income rose 4 percent year on year to SGD 3.711 billion. Hedging and balance-sheet growth helped offset the impact of lower Singapore Overnight Rate Average levels. Net interest margin was 1.87 percent in the quarter.

Net fee income increased 6 percent to SGD 1.432 billion. Wealth management fees rose 9 percent to SGD 864 million, while assets under management reached a record SGD 544 billion after strong net new money inflows. Commercial-book other non-interest income rose 19 percent to SGD 685 million, supported mainly by treasury customer sales.

The broader nine-month picture remained stronger than the quarterly headline. Net profit for the first nine months rose 2 percent to a record SGD 8.822 billion, while total income increased 2 percent to SGD 17.886 billion. Return on equity was 17.0 percent, and the non-performing-loan ratio improved to 0.9 percent at the end of September.

For 2027, DBS expects total income growth in the mid-single-digit range. The outlook assumes two further US Federal Reserve rate increases by the end of next year, average SORA of about 1.6 percent and a stronger Singapore dollar. The bank expects loan and deposit growth to support net interest income, while structural expansion in wealth management should continue.

Chief executive Tan Su Shan said the global outlook had become more uncertain because of elevated energy prices, tighter financial conditions and geopolitical risks. She said DBS would remain nimble while managing risks, with capital, liquidity and general allowance buffers providing resilience.

sum: DBS Group reported a weaker third quarter on November 5, as a sharp decline in markets trading income outweighed continued growth in wealth management and fee income. CNA reported that net profit for the July-to-September period fell 5 percent year on year to S$2.81 billion, below the S$2.90 billion average forecast from four analysts surveyed by LSEG.

The main drag came from markets trading income, which plunged 65 percent from a year earlier to S$152 million. DBS attributed the decline to unfavourable equity market conditions, while its net interest margin narrowed by nine basis points to 1.87 percent.

The result also shows that the bank's customer franchises continued to provide support. Wealth management fees increased 9 percent year on year to S$864 million, and net fee income rose 6 percent to S$1.43 billion. Those gains were not enough to offset the trading setback, leaving investors to weigh the durability of customer-led growth against more volatile markets revenue.

DBS expects total income to rise in the mid-single-digit range in 2027. Management said structural growth in wealth management should continue, while Chief Executive Tan Su Shan cautioned that the global outlook had become more uncertain because of market and geopolitical risks.

For investors, the earnings mix is important. The quarter showed that lending profitability and wealth-related fees can cushion weaker capital-markets activity, but it also highlighted the sensitivity of quarterly earnings to trading conditions. The next results will indicate whether fee growth and balance-sheet expansion can keep offsetting pressure on markets income and margins.

items.t: Banco Do Brasil Shares Slid Even Though Sales Rose
sum: Brazil's state controlled lender just reported Q2 2026 results showing revenue at R$21,915.374m and net income at R$2,397.643m, with net margin at 10.9% versus 12.7% a year earlier. Holding Banco do Brasil over the past year would have meant a 22.5% loss, including dividends. If you had bought on 6 November 2025, that headline number is the experience to explain. The open question now is whether current profitability justifies renewed optimism about its digital and agribusiness initiatives.
If the move has made Banco do Brasil harder to judge, start where the gap is still open and scan 217 high quality undervalued stocks.
The shares cost R$22.86 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Banco do Brasil then had to choose between two very different scripts.

The bullish story saw digital acceleration and a rising middle class reshaping the bank, with a Fair Value of R$39, a price that assumed revenue could grow 12.7% a year and eSocial driven payroll lending would scale rapidly.
The cautious view argued fintech rivalry and regulation might bite harder, with a Fair Value of R$20 based on 8.9% revenue growth and persistent asset quality pressure in agribusiness and MSMEs.

The clearest new fact is that Banco do Brasil's Q2 2026 revenue sat at R$21,915.374m versus R$21,873.133m a year earlier. Net income moved from R$2,782.083m to R$2,397.643m and net margin slipped from 12.7% to 10.9%. That pattern of slightly higher sales but thinner profitability leaned toward the cautious script that worried about pressure on earnings quality.

The useful takeaway for any bank you follow is simple. When a bullish pitch hangs on improving efficiency and profitability, check whether net income and net margin move in the same direction as revenue in later results, not just whether the top line holds steady.

Singapore Banks Face Slower Growth in 2027 as Deposit Competition Bites
sum: Analysts expect Singapore’s banks to face slower growth in 2027 as deposit competition squeezes margins and wealth fees weaken. The outlook follows mixed third-quarter results: OCBC beat estimates, while DBS and UOB fell short. Analysts say the banks remain on different footing.

Singapore’s three largest banks may see slower growth in 2027 as deposit competition and weaker wealth fees pressure earnings, analysts said after mixed third-quarter results. The outlook matters to investors tracking the banks’ performance as DBS and UOB missed analysts’ expectations, while OCBC beat them.
“The boom years did a lot of the work for Singapore’s banks,” said Eric Xiao, head of sales in Asia for CMC Markets. “In 2027, they’ll have to do it themselves.”

Xiao said DBS took in a record S$15 billion (US$11.7 billion) of net new money in the third quarter, but wealth fees fell 6 per cent as clients traded less. He said monetizing the wealth boom appeared more difficult than expected.

Higher interest rates could eventually help banks, Xiao said, but margins may initially come under pressure because deposit rates tend to rise faster than loan rates. He did not expect a “down year” for the banks despite the tougher conditions.

Ritesh Ganeriwal, group head of investment and advisory at Syfe, said the banks’ core business held up in the third quarter, but “the problem is that interest rates are no longer doing the heavy lifting”.

Singapore rates have remained low even as US rates rise, while banks compete harder for deposits, Ganeriwal said. He expects slower growth in 2027, driven by loans and wealth fees, rather than a downturn.

sum: On October 30, 2026: price 73.13 SGD, trend downtrend, RSI 33.1, support 73.13, resistance 78.56. technical analysis of dbs stock. DBS Stock Drops — full…

DBS Group closed at S$73.13 on Friday, October 30, 2026, down 0.91% for the session and 1.76% over five days. The stock is close to its three-month low of S$72.50 while its decline continues, putting the focus on whether selling pressure eases near the bottom of the recent range. The latest session’s volume was 1.3 times its 20-day average, while on-balance volume fell—a sign that heavier trading has not yet confirmed a shift in demand.

The short-term structure remains weak. DBS traded below its 20-day moving average of S$74.66, which itself fell 1.29% over five days, and below its 50-day average of S$76.23. No new moving-average crossover was reported. The lack of a fresh crossover does not alter the underlying message: price and the shorter-term average remain beneath the longer-term reference, while the short-term average is declining.

The price sat at the bottom of its 20-trading-day range, between support at S$73.13 and resistance at S$78.56. The three-month low of S$72.50 is nearby, but proximity to a low is not, by itself, evidence of a reversal. The session’s close also matches the stated 20-day support level, making the next response around this zone especially relevant.
As shown in the chart, price is positioned below both moving averages and near the lower part of the recent range.

The indicators show weakness, but not a uniform signal of an established rebound. The RSI is 33.1, classified as neutral in the supplied data; it is close to the lower end of the scale, but does not independently confirm a turn. The Stochastic is oversold, with %K at 14.5 and %D at 34.1. That can occur when selling has been persistent; an oversold reading is not a timing signal unless price and momentum begin to recover.

The MACD remains negative: at -0.766, it is below its -0.708 signal line, and its histogram is -0.058. This points to negative momentum rather than a confirmed bullish divergence. Taken together, the readings suggest the stock may be stretched near support, while the broader momentum picture still leans downward.

The MSCI EM Asia equities index declined 1.8% in its worst day since early September, largely weighed down by a 2.6% drop in South Korea's Kospi.

In Singapore, the FTSE Straits Times index shed as much as 3.2% to hit its lowest since mid-July, with DBS dipping 5.2% to mark its steepest daily loss since April last year. Smaller rivals OCBC and UOB fell nearly 5% each. Together, the three banks account for more than half of Singapore's main index, and make up more than a third of the MSCI Asean equity gauge, which marked its worst daily drop since early March.

JPMorgan and Citi raised concerns over Asean banks' earnings outlook, citing surging long-dated bond yields, higher funding costs and the normalisation of exceptional first-half wealth-related income.

"A combination of higher rates, AQ (asset quality) risks, funding tightness and capital-market-related revenue risks should impact quite a few bank stocks going into 3Q results," JPMorgan analysts led by Harsh Wardhan Modi wrote.
They recommend trimming exposure to all three major Singapore banks.

DBS shares rally to new high of $55.54 as Q3 earnings beat expectations
sum: SINGAPORE - Shares of DBS surged past $55 for the first time on Nov 6 after Singapore’s largest bank posted a smaller-than-expected drop in third-quarter earnings as lower interest rates squeeze margins.

The stock opened at $53.90, crossed the $55 mark at 9.15am and continued to rise throughout the day. At the close of trading, DBS was up 3.8 per cent or $2.04 to $55.54, after 13.1 million shares changed hands.

The bank’s net profit for the three months to Sept 30 dipped 2 per cent to $2.95 billion, from $3.03 billion in the year-ago period, but beat the $2.79 billion forecast by analysts in a Bloomberg poll.
The bank declared an interim one-tier dividend of 60 cents and a one-tier capital return dividend of 15 cents for each ordinary share.
This brings the quarter’s total dividend payout to 75 cents per share, compared with the 54 cents in the year-ago period.
DBS said commercial book net interest income in the quarter fell 6 per cent to $3.56 billion as lower rates were mitigated by hedging and deposit growth.
Commercial book net interest margin declined 43 basis points to 2.4 per cent, from 2.83 per cent in the year-ago period.

DBS hits new record of $55.55 with higher dividend commitment
sum: DBS Group Holdings' share price hit a new record of $55.55 after it reported better-than-expected 3QFY2025 earnings. A commitment to increase its already generous dividend payout for the coming FY2026 sent the bank's market cap above $157 billion.

In the coming year, DBS plans to increase its quarterly ordinary dividend payout by 6 cents to 66 cents, which means an additional 24 cents for FY2026. In addition, there's 15 cents per share to be paid in capital return dividend, which has been committed up to FY2027, which works out to 81 cents per quarter.
"We will get it approved at the AGM in March 2026, and then it will actually flow through," says CFO Chng Sok Hui at the bank's results briefing.
Based on DBS's current full-year dividend of $3, comprising 60 cents ordinary dividend and 15 cents capital return per quarter, the dividend yield works out at 5.4%.
"We've always said that we had $8 billion of excess stock of capital to return. We remain committed to returning that," says CEO Tan Su Shan at the same briefing.
Of this $8 billion, $3 billion has been allocated to share buybacks and thus far, 12% of that amount spent.
"Our philosophy is to buy when the market is bad," says Tan.
